findings.what_is_wrong: The old maskSecrets (rules M2, M8, M9) hid in result files, as I ran on the base clone: API_KEY=..., api_key: "...", secret=..., token=..., passwd=..., authorization=..., a literal after Bearer outside an Authorization header, and any value of Authorization: (for example Basic). The new refusal set of criteria 3/11 (C1-C9) holds only password=<literal> and Authorization: Bearer <literal> from these families. So api_key=/secret=/token=/passwd=/apikey= with a real literal value, and non-Bearer Authorization values, are now stored in files/ and handed to the reviewer unprotected, while the description says the protection is not weaker. The residual-risk wording ('секрет без префикса и без метки имени') even suggests that labelled secrets are caught, but no criterion says which names are labels. Step 9 cannot decide whether api_key=<literal> must be refused. Quality bar section 1: the bar is not lowered by a task text.
findings.needed_to_pass: Decide, by the author and with ORCH where it is a choice (record in decisions/ per Q12), for each dropped form (name=value pairs of the M9 names, Bearer outside the header, other Authorization schemes): either it is refused and has a refuse sample and a keep sample on the criterion 1 / criterion 3 boundary (O6 `{ token: data.token, user: x }` must keep being stored), or the narrowing is named as an accepted residual risk in the description and criterion 11(b) and the claim 'не слабеет, а строже' is corrected. findings.place: criterion 7 (line 12599), families (1), (4), (6); mutant m5 in criterion 10 (line 12624)
findings.what_is_wrong: The ratio of the time at 4 MiB to the time at 1 MiB measures the scan only if the scan runs to the end of the input. Family (1) is `-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----` repeated without END, which by criterion 3 sample C5 (second form) is a refused input, so a findSecrets that returns at the first match is constant time and the ratio is timer noise of microsecond values (the test can be red or green by chance, and the pressure to loosen it is a Q6 risk). Families (4) (the first three repeated `eyJ...` parts already form a JWT shape) and (6) (`password="a...` is a literal value) can hit at the start in the same way. Then mutant m5 (quadratic end search) may not be killed by the named test, so criterion 10 cannot be answered with yes/no for m5. The criterion does not say what the function returns for these inputs nor that the whole input must be scanned.
findings.needed_to_pass: Define the families so that every measured input holds no secret (or define the measured work so that it cannot stop at a first hit), say which family kills m5, and give the measurement a floor so that the compared times are not noise. The instrument control (quadratic reference function) stays.

issues.text: For ORCH and the owner (F1): the old masking hid name=value secrets (api_key, secret, token, passwd, apikey), Bearer outside a header and any Authorization value in result files. Do you accept that result-file detection is narrowed to the CORE-0 list plus password= and Authorization: Bearer (decision 0102 item 11), or must the refused set also cover those name forms? This is a choice between protection and false refusals of ordinary code; it needs a record in decisions/ either way (Q12).
